items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter names in business logic: `f`, `d`, `M`, `h`, `w`, `sx`, `sy`, `py0/px1/ry0`. Casing is inconsistent (`valid_Indices`). No docstrings on any function. Some comments help, e.g. "Find jump apex" and "Compensate for illumination drift".

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `analyze_video` is about 155 lines (over the 100-line cap) and mixes capture, alignment, segmentation and takeoff/landing logic. The pre/post ground logic is copy-pasted. Dead comment: "Check if push-off peak is 1 frame earlier". Odd `cv2.sys.argv` / `cv2.os.path` hacks.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Checks `cap.isOpened()`, raises on an unreadable first frame and on "No athlete detected", and falls back on fps. But it has many magic constants (1225, 380, 220, 180.0, 140/820, 3000) with no rationale. `cap` is released manually, not via try/finally.

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: Validates opening and raises ValueError/RuntimeError, so the exit is non-zero, though with a traceback rather than a clean message. Thresholds are absolute pixel constants scaled from 960x540 (`dist2 > 1225`, `min_athlete_area`), not derived from the background.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Takes the first positional argv as the video and always writes /app/output.toml with exactly `jump_takeoff_frame_number` and `jump_land_frame_number` as ints. Frame indexing is consistently 0-based (first frame = 0, loop starts at 1). All hidden tests pass.
